selectionNotes: Select one of the two complete 2020 ATLAS convex models, 4625 (188,32). The counterpart 4626 (3,16) remains possible. The independent 2021 ASAS-SN pole (187,21) supports the same broad family but is not the selected mesh or an exact attitude validation.
sourceLimitations: The pinned mesh is an inverse model, not a directly sampled surface. No registered reflectance mosaic is supplied by this release; a neutral grid must mark unavailable imagery. Fine-scale craters, regolith and albedo are unresolved. Absolute rotational phase is illustrative. Select one of the two complete 2020 ATLAS convex models, 4625 (188,32). The counterpart 4626 (3,16) remains possible. The independent 2021 ASAS-SN pole (187,21) supports the same broad family but is not the selected mesh or an exact attitude validation.
calibrationSelection: Pinned AKARI AcuA v1.0 thermal effective-sphere diameter is assigned to mesh volume only as an explicit display-scale approximation; formal catalog errors omit additional shape, spin and thermal-model systematics.
sourceCoordinatePreservation: Original counted shape bytes, coordinates, vertex order, face order and one-based connectivity are retained unchanged. One preparation-owned uniform scale maps original coordinates to km.

visibleShapeDescription: Convex light-curve reconstruction with approximate thermal size: 42.18 km (catalog ±0.49 km; additional shape and thermal-model uncertainty). Thermal size is used as a volume-scale approximation. An alternative pole remains possible. The grid marks unavailable imagery.

calibration.uncertaintyKind: Formal catalog uncertainty; excludes extra shape, spin and thermal-model systematics. It is not the total uncertainty of the displayed physical scale.
calibration.additionalSystematics: Usui2011§2.3 explicitly omits unquantified shape/spin/thermal-model effects; rotation can add a few to about10%in size, especially for fewdetections. No invented numerical confidence interval is assigned to these unquantified effects.
calibration.diameterSemantics: Mean fitted diameter of a nonrotating sphere in the modified Standard Thermal Model. Its use as the volume-equivalent diameter of the separate convex DAMIT mesh is an explicit display-scale approximation, not a published physical-volume calibration.
calibration.limitations: The physical size is approximately calibrated by assigning the AKARI thermal effective diameter to the mesh volume-equivalent diameter. Neither source mesh nor spin is modified. Convex inversion supplies only broad outline; no resolved craters, concavities, reflectance or regolith texture can be inferred. Select one of the two complete 2020 ATLAS convex models, 4625 (188,32). The counterpart 4626 (3,16) remains possible. The independent 2021 ASAS-SN pole (187,21) supports the same broad family but is not the selected mesh or an exact attitude validation.
